title: setRewardToken silently re-keys the nudge stream and permanently bricks claim(), the sole permissionless entry point
fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:setRewardToken:undocumented-re-arm-trigger-for-cross-contract-liveness-precondition-mandatory-external-dependency-fallback-removed)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]
description: setRewardToken is an undocumented re-arm trigger for the mandatory-streamer brick, and is the only load-bearing address setter that emits no event -- Total, permanent-until-cured outage of claim(), which is the only permissionless entry point and the sole mechanism converting yield-strategy surplus into phlimbo rewards. Verified constructively: revert selector 0xd62cbfe8 (NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered()), with a direct storage assertion that the old (sink, oldReward) stream survives with duration == DURATION while (sink, newReward) has duration == 0 — nothing broke, the KEY MOVED. Warping 365 days and retrying reverts identically.
impact: Total, permanent-until-cured outage of claim(), which is the only permissionless entry point and the sole mechanism converting yield-strategy surplus into phlimbo rewards. Verified constructively: revert selector 0xd62cbfe8 (NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered()), with a direct storage assertion that the old (sink, oldReward) stream survives with duration == DURATION while (sink, newReward) has duration == 0 — nothing broke, the KEY MOVED. Warping 365 days and retrying reverts identically.
assetImpact: NONE. No assets are stolen, lost or compromised on this path. Tier-3 Property 3 verified constructively that a nudge-leg revert rolls back the entire claim — the claimer's payment, skimmed surplus, NFT burn and streamer deposit all revert together, so no partial-state value loss is reachable.
attackPath: No attacker exists. This is an owner-footgun path, not an exploit.
1. System is live and correctly configured per the in-source runbook (:82-90); claims succeed and move value on every leg (Tier-3 positive control).
2. Owner rotates the reward denomination: setRewardToken(newToken) — a bare assignment at :417-420 with a zero-address check, no rail guard, and no event.
3. Every subsequent claim() carrying a payable nudge share reverts NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered().

4. The outage persists until the owner performs an ORDERED two-call repair on two OTHER contracts: setNudgeTokenWhitelist(newToken, true) on the batch minter, then registerStream(nudge, newToken, duration) on the streamer. Reversing that order reverts NudgeStreamer__NotWhitelisted (0x0dc85695).
recommendation: Gate setRewardToken on nudgeSplit == 0, OR have it staticcall INudgeStreamer for a registered (nudge, newToken) stream and revert otherwise. At minimum: emit RewardTokenUpdated(old, new); add setRewardToken to the ops NatSpec as failure mode 4; and zero the stale phlimbo allowance on repoint (see L-05).
aggravators: SILENT: setRewardToken is the ONLY load-bearing address setter in the contract with no event — setPauser, setPhlimbo, setNudgeAddress, setNudgeSplit, setNudgeStreamer, setNFTMinter, setTokenConfig and setDiscountRate all emit. Off-chain monitoring cannot see the state change, converting a detectable outage into a silently-initiated one. (Detection still occurs quickly via user-facing reverts, which is why this is an aggravator and not an escalator.)

DOCUMENTATION MAKES IT NON-OBVIOUS: the contract NatSpec (:69-79) presents a CLOSED enumeration — 'there are three failure modes' — and names only setNudgeAddress as a re-arm trigger. An owner following the documented runbook to the letter still bricks the rail. Verified first-hand at f704130.

SECOND BLAST LEG: the same call strands the standing approvePhlimbo allowance, which remains denominated in the OLD token, breaking the phlimbo leg independently of the streamer leg. Generalized as L-05.
law3Ruling: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun, NOT suppressed as a reckless-admin mistake. Surprise test: a competent, non-malicious owner rotating the reward denomination would be surprised that claim() dies, because the document that enumerates the re-arm triggers omits this one. Classified by the impact it unlocks (an availability outage), per the operational-hazard rule.
likelihood: low-to-moderate for the trigger (reward-denomination rotation is a real but infrequent ops action; the project has a documented history of repointing contracts), HIGH for the consequence given the trigger, since the brick is unconditional and immediate.
assumptions: nudgeSplit > 0 (the live-donation branch). With nudgeSplit == 0 the whole streamer requirement is bypassed and the finding does not arise.
externalRequirements: Repair requires onlyOwner calls on NudgeStreamer and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken — contracts SYA does not control. Resolved as the SAME owner key (SWING-001), so this is an ordering burden, not a cross-party coordination burden.
